correctness.rationale: The theorem is correct. For a part i the open-neighborhood sum is total weight minus the part weight and its smallest positive feasible value is the parity-adjusted epsilon_i. Flipping a positive vertex leaves its own part's open-neighborhood sum unchanged and lowers every other part by two, so a signed total dominating function is minimal exactly when every part containing a positive vertex has a different tight part. With two tight parts, their two part-weight bounds and the remaining-vertices bound give the three stated ceilings. A unique tight part can only produce weight at most one and cannot maximize. For any chosen pair, parity makes the bottleneck target attainable in the two tight parts and on the remaining vertices while preserving every other inequality, giving equality. Fresh independent brute force through total order eight agreed with the formula and the tight-part criterion.
